Josephine Platner Shear (3 July 1901 - 11 February 1967) was an American classical archaeologist and numismatist, known for her leadership in both excavation and numismatic studies during the Agora excavations.

Biography

Josephine Platner was born on 3 July 1901 in Omaha, Nebraska. She graduated from Wellesley College in 1924 and pursued further studies in archaeology at Columbia University, completing her education in 1928.

From 1927 to 1929 and again from 1931 to 1939, Platner was a member of the American School of Classical Studies at Athens. In the year 1939-1940, she was awarded a fellowship at the same institution. Between 1929 and 1931, Platner participated in the Corinth excavations. In 1930, she presented her research on geometric pottery from Corinth to the Archaeological Institute of America.

On 12 February 1931, she married archaeologist Theodore Leslie Shear (1880-1945), who led the Corinth excavations from 1925 to 1931 and initiated the Agora excavations in Athens in 1931. Although Theodore Shear was the nominal Director of the Corinth excavations, it was Josephine Platner Shear who oversaw the actual digging operations. The plans she created for the excavation remain influential references in the field.

While her husband was at Princeton, Platner Shear worked alongside him and also contributed to academic life through lectures, including a notable one to the Women's College Club in 1936. During the Agora excavations, she took charge of studying and conserving the numismatic finds from the site. Her work led to the discovery of a previously unknown 2nd-century C.E. Athenian coin.

Platner Shear maintained meticulous records of the numismatic material; during the 1937 season alone, she catalogued 10,325 coins. Among the significant finds of that year was a silver obol of Solon, identified by Platner Shear.

After her husband's death in 1945, she continued to reside in Princeton. In 1955, she married Floyd C. Harwood. Josephine Platner Shear passed away on 11 February 1967. Objects she excavated are now part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's collection.

Bee populations are facing a serious threat, known as Colony Collapse Disorder (CCD), which is caused by a mix of factors. Imagine if our busy little bee friends started disappearing mysteriously, it would have a huge impact on our world too. Pesticides, especially neonicotinoids, are one major issue. These sneaky chemicals seep into every part of the plant, even the nectar and pollen that bees feed on. This exposure can confuse bees, weaken their immune systems, and even mess with their ability to reproduce.

Another challenge for bees is habitat loss. As humans, we tend to take up a lot of space, turning natural habitats into cities, farms, and other developments. This not only destroys the homes of many bees, but also reduces the variety of flowers they rely on for food. Monoculture farming, where only one type of crop is grown, makes things even worse by limiting the kind of nectar and pollen available.

Diseases and parasites are yet another hurdle. Varroa destructor mites, for instance, latch onto bees, feed on them, and spread viruses, causing deformities in developing bees. Climate change and shifting weather patterns don't help either. They can disrupt bee behavior and the timing of plant blooming.

There's hope, though! We can all do our part to help our buzzing buddies. Reducing pesticide use, creating and preserving bee habitats, and promoting bee-friendly farming practices are great steps. On a smaller scale, planting native flowers, cutting down on lawn size, and providing nesting sites can make a difference. Supporting organic farming and advocating for policies that protect natural habitats and limit pesticide use can also go a long way in saving the bees.

Imagine two cosmic monsters, each born from the collision of matter and antimatter, their gravity so strong that not even light can escape. They're hurtling towards each other, and we're left wondering what will happen when they collide. Will they merge into an even bigger beast, or will they annihilate each other in a spectacular display of energy release? The answer is far from simple, and it's a puzzle that has puzzled physicists for years.

To unravel this mystery, we need to delve into the fundamental laws of physics, from general relativity to quantum mechanics. Black holes, as regions of spacetime, are characterized by their mass, spin, and charge. But here's the twist - a black hole formed from matter has positive mass and energy, while one formed from antimatter has negative mass and energy.

When these two black holes meet, several scenarios unfold. They might undergo annihilation, canceling each other out and releasing a massive amount of energy in the form of gamma rays and other radiation. But this process wouldn't be complete, as some energy and momentum would be conserved.

Alternatively, the two black holes might merge, but not in a straightforward way. The laws of general relativity predict that gravitational waves would arise, carrying away some of the energy and momentum. The resulting black hole would likely be smaller than the sum of its parts, due to the energy lost as radiation.

However, when we gaze through the lens of quantum mechanics, things get even more intriguing. The 'no-hair theorem' suggests that a black hole has only three hairs: mass, spin, and charge. Since the matter and antimatter black holes have opposite charges, their merger could result in a black hole with zero charge - a truly unusual object.

Moreover, the collision could create a multitude of new particles and antiparticles, potentially even new forms of matter and energy we've never seen before. Particle-antiparticle pairs could be created near the event horizon, further complicating the merger process.

In conclusion, the collision of a matter-based black hole and an antimatter-based black hole would be an awe-inspiring event, with a multitude of possible outcomes. It's unlikely to result in a bigger black hole, but rather a rich tapestry of energy releases, particle creations, and potentially even new forms of matter and energy. The universe is full of mysteries, and this is certainly one of them.

Researchers have studied these moths to understand their habits, behavior, and how to manage them. They've found that the larvae are attracted to the chemicals emitted by Galapagos palm leaves and that a combination of insecticides and biological control agents can reduce their population. 

Aristotelia palamota is an important moth species with significant economic and environmental implications, especially in the Galapagos Islands. Further research is needed to develop effective ways to manage this pest."

Preserving the tree of life: the key role of phylogenetic diversity in conservation planning"

The rapid loss of biodiversity we are currently experiencing threatens not only the natural world, but also the stability and resilience of the ecosystems we rely on. While we have made progress in protecting species richness, we have yet to fully understand and address the implications of losing phylogenetic diversity (PD) - the evolutionary history and distinctness of species within an ecosystem.

To fill this gap, we have developed a new method for estimating the expected contribution of species to future PD. By integrating phylogenetic and demographic models, we can construct a phylogenetic tree for a set of species and simulate their evolutionary dynamics over time. This allows us to calculate the expected PD at each time step, and identify which species are most important in maintaining PD in the long term.

Our findings highlight the critical importance of considering both species richness and PD when planning conservation efforts. By prioritizing the conservation of species that are expected to contribute significantly to future PD, we can ensure the sustainability of ecosystems and the services they provide. This not only helps protect the natural world, but also safeguards our own future.

In short, our work provides a valuable new tool for preserving the richness and diversity of life on Earth. By hedging our bets on the species that will contribute most to PD, we can ensure that the tree of life continues to thrive for generations to come.

Anxiety attacks are rooted in a primal "fight or flight" response to perceived danger. When triggered, your body floods with adrenaline, leading to various physical symptoms like a racing heart, rapid breathing, tingling sensations, and muscle tension.  While these physical sensations occur during an attack, feelings of dread or doom often precede them, stemming from past trauma or deep-seated anxieties. 

Our brains learn from these experiences, sometimes misinterpreting similar situations as threats. This can create a cycle where even benign triggers, like being in a moving vehicle after associating it with past nausea, can induce anxiety. 

This cycle is often amplified by obsessive thoughts and anxiety disorders. The inability to sleep, for instance, can fuel anxiety, which further prevents sleep.  This creates a frustrating loop of worry and physical symptoms.

Interestingly, anxiety attacks aren't always triggered by external events. Internal factors, such as gut health issues like acid reflux or an imbalance in gut flora, are being studied for their potential links to anxiety. 

While anxiety is a common human experience, people with heightened sensitivity to internal or external stimuli and those prone to obsessive thoughts may experience it more severely. If anxiety significantly impacts your life, seeking professional help is crucial. 

Coping mechanisms like meditation and focused breathing can be immensely helpful. Concentrate on each inhale and exhale, taking slow, deep breaths. This technique can calm your nervous system and alleviate the intensity of an attack. Remember, you're not alone in this, and effective strategies for managing anxiety exist. Don't hesitate to seek support and discover what works best for you.

On most slave vessels, the standard practice was to bring out small groups of enslaved individuals during good weather onto the ship's deck to eat, be cleaned, and have some limited exercise. The most famous form of exercise was making slaves dance and sing on the spot, though this was not a universal practice. The food provided had little real nutritional value, either for adults or growing children. Typical concoctions included mushed beans or rice acquired on the West African coast, made into a seasoned pulp that might, if one were 'lucky,' contain a little meat. Most slave ships carried enough food to ensure a minimum level of rationing in the event of spoilage. Water was distributed in strictly rationed quantities two to three times a day, usually alongside food, at about half a pint.

If the weather did not permit bringing captives on deck for feeding, food would be distributed in communal tubs in confinement areas. If an individual African refused to eat or desired to commit suicide by starvation, they could be 'safely' force-fed using a scissor-like medical instrument designed to hold open the human jaw. Given the conditions of malnutrition and dehydration, however, most enslaved persons would have welcomed the little food and water provided, especially after several days on board.

Large wooden or metal buckets were provided for slaves to relieve themselves, but given that they were kept manacled at all times, this was often impractical. It was common for slaves to be forced to relieve themselves within their holding areas. Some effort was made to clean both individuals and confinement areas on most slave ships, but this was not always possible or practical, especially on ships with a shortage of crew due to sailor deaths from malnutrition and disease.

Feeding, cleaning, and exercise time theoretically provided an opportunity to identify Africans succumbing to illness and remove them to other parts of the ship, if space permitted. In practice, however, this strategy was ineffective, as any illness was likely a result of the appalling conditions. Problems were compounded by the fact that some Africans would vomit bile and blood from sickness or have open sores and wounds that could leak.

In terms of mortality, it is impossible to know precisely how many individuals lost their lives during the transatlantic slave trade. The best estimate, based on comprehensive surveys of surviving records of slave vessels for all major European powers, puts the total number of African men, women, and children who died making the journey on slave ships to the New World at over 1.82 million between 1501 and 1866, though the true figure could certainly be higher. Generally, the pattern shows declining mortality during this period as European governments responded to abolitionist critique, and slave traders sought to maximize the survivability rates of their human cargo.

For vessels flying British or American flags, the mortality rates were as follows by half-century:
* 1501 - 1600: 29%
* 1601 - 1650: 22%
* 1651 - 1700: 24%
* 1700 - 1750: 18%
* 1751 - 1800: 14%
* 1800 - 1850: 13%
^Figures ^taken ^from ^the ^Transatlantic ^Slave ^Trade ^Database

Note that both Britain and the United States abolished the slave trade after 1807, though it continued in an illicit form for some years afterward. The British/American slave trade alone killed nearly 600,000 people, in addition to the 2.9 million it successfully delivered into slavery in the New World. The Atlantic Ocean became a literal burial ground for millions of African men, women, boys, and girls whose lives were claimed by malnutrition, disease, and violence.

The brutal experience of the Middle Passage was not accidental. Although slave vessels had a vested interest in delivering as many people as possible to the New World, the process of degradation was part of the system by which slavers hoped to break the spirit and sense of human dignity in their victims. It was inherently violent, intended to demonstrate to Africans how little they were worth in the eyes of their captors and to enforce their place in the racially stratified social order of the New World.

The popular image of the slave trade is somewhat inaccurate. On British slave vessels, standard practice was to keep adult men chained below decks, while adult women and girls were kept in a separate holding area without the same physical restraints. Young boys were either kept separately or with the women. Young male children often had the most liberal experience of captivity, being permitted some roaming freedom. However, women and children were at constant risk of sexual exploitation and gratuitous violence from the crew.

Africans did not simply accept their fate. Many sought to resist their captors through small acts of autonomy, such as using the relative freedom of children to ferry messages, to full violent insurrections. We know of hundreds of acts of violent resistance, including dozens of major uprisings on slave vessels. These acts of resistance highlight the white European fear of African agency. Despite attempts to destroy African identity, captors were aware of their captives' determined and resistant spirit.

Two recommended books for understanding the slave trade in an engaging and accessible fashion are Audra Diptee's "From Africa to Jamaica: The Making of an Atlantic Slave Society, 1775 - 1807," which argues that slave traders could not ignore the humanity of African people, and James Walvin's "The Zong: A Massacre, The Law and the End of Slavery," which offers insights from the infamous Zong massacre. Both books benefit from recent developments in the historiography of the transatlantic slave trade and should be widely accessible.

The Multiband Imaging Photometer for Spitzer (MIPS) has been recalibrated and characterized, with a focus on the 24 micron band and the stellar calibrator sample. Previously, the lack of accurate calibration led to systematic errors, particularly at 24 micron. To address this, we re-examined the stellar calibrator sample of 36 objects with well-known fluxes, re-deriving their 24 micron fluxes using contemporaneous Infrared Array Camera data. By building a spectral energy distribution for each calibrator, we assessed the accuracy of the MIPS 24 micron calibration, reducing the systematic error from 10% to 3%. We developed a new method to determine the instrumental response function, quantifying the contribution of various components to the total error budget. This work provides a reliable foundation for MIPS data analysis, enabling precise measurements of galaxy properties. Our calibration approach can be applied to future space-based missions, highlighting the importance of accurate absolute calibration for achieving reliable scientific results.

Back in the 1600s and 1700s, Europeans went crazy for beaver hats! They loved the soft pelts so much that a huge fur trade sprang up in North America.  But even though everyone was clamoring for those pelts, no one really tried to domesticate beavers like they did with other animals.  

Here's why:

* **Beavers are Really Smart (and a bit of a handful):** They're not your typical farm animal. Beavers are like the Einsteins of the rodent world. They live in big, organized families with complicated rules about building dams and protecting their territory. Imagine trying to wrangle a bunch of super-smart architects all living by the water – it's a recipe for chaos!

* **Momma Beaver and Her Babies:** Beavers have babies pretty quickly, but those babies need a whole lot of love and attention for a long time.  It would've been really tough and expensive to recreate that in a farm setting.  It was just easier to catch them in the wild.

* **Fur Takes a Lottery:** Unlike with other animals, where everyone's fur is pretty much the same, beaver fur can vary a lot depending on the beaver's age, the season, and even its genes.  It made it harder to build a steady supply of top-notch fur from captive beavers.

* **Plenty of Beavers, Plenty of Places to Live:** Beavers were still pretty common in North America even during the fur trade.  They had tons of space to roam and build their dams, so there was no real need to domesticate them. Trapping them in the wild was a lot simpler.


Remember, even though trapping was a big part of the beaver fur trade, it was the massive overhunting and loss of their homes that nearly wiped them out.  Thankfully, people eventually realized they needed to protect these amazing animals."

How to Make Rustic Bread

Rustic bread is a delicious, crusty loaf that goes well with meals or makes a great snack. It has a chewy inside and a crispy, golden-brown crust. Baking this bread at home is a fun and rewarding experience that will make your home smell amazing and taste buds happy.

Gather Your Ingredients:
You’ll need the following for 4-5 loaves:
- 3 cups lukewarm water
- 1.5 tablespoons active dry yeast
- 1.5 tablespoons sea salt
- 6.5 cups unbleached white flour

Step-by-Step Instructions:

1. **Mix Your Ingredients**:
   - Pour the lukewarm water (around 100°F or 38°C) into a large mixing bowl.
   - Sprinkle the yeast evenly over the water.
   - Add the sea salt.
   - Slowly mix in all the flour.

2. **Combine Everything**:
   - Use a stand mixer with a dough hook on medium-low speed until the dough is sticky and well combined.

3. **Let the Dough Rise**:
   - Cover the bowl with a clean tea towel or plastic wrap.
   - Let it rise in a warm spot (75-85°F or 24-29°C) for about 2 hours, until it doubles in size.

4. **Prepare to Bake**:
   - Preheat your oven to 450°F (225°C).

5. **Shape Your Dough**:
   - Dust a surface with flour and take a piece of dough about the size of a small melon.
   - Knead it for about 1 minute until it's more elastic.
   - Shape it into a round, oval or long form and place it on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
   - Let it rise again for 20-30 minutes.

6. **Bake Your Bread**:
   - Place the baking sheet in the preheated oven and bake for 25-30 minutes until the bread is golden brown.
   - Tap the crust; if it sounds hollow, it's done.

7. **Cool and Serve**:
   - Let the bread cool on a rack before slicing.
   - Enjoy your homemade bread with butter, cheese, cold cuts, jam, or dipped in olive oil with sea salt.

Distance learning, often referred to as online learning or e-learning, has become an increasingly popular alternative to traditional classroom education. This growth can be attributed to advances in technology, increased accessibility to the internet, and an increased recognition of its potential to provide quality education to students who face various challenges. Among these challenges are bullying, lengthy commutes, and low attendance rates. In this essay, I will argue that distance learning offers several benefits that can help mitigate these obstacles and enhance students' overall educational experience, using supporting evidence from literature and media.

Firstly, distance learning provides a safe environment for students who are victims of bullying. Bullying is a pervasive issue affecting countless students worldwide, causing emotional and psychological distress. According to a report by the National Center for Education Statistics (2019), nearly 22% of students between the ages of 12 and 18 reported being bullied at school. Distance learning offers a solution for these students by allowing them to learn in a secure and comfortable space, free from the negative social pressures that often result in bullying. For instance, the documentary 'Bully' (2011) highlights the struggles of several students who face bullying and the impact it has on their academic performance and overall well-being. Distance learning can help these students achieve academic success without the fear of being bullied.

Secondly, distance learning significantly reduces commuting time for students, particularly those living in rural areas or those with long journeys to and from school. According to a report by the National Center for Education Statistics (2017), approximately 11% of students aged 14 and older spend more than an hour commuting to school. Distance learning eliminates this time spent traveling and allows students to allocate it towards productive activities such as studying, hobbies, or even part-time employment. Online platforms provide students with the flexibility to learn from the comfort of their homes, regardless of their geographical location. A study by the National Bureau of Economic Research (2020) found that students who took distance learning courses were less likely to drop out of school and had higher overall academic performance.

Lastly, distance learning has the potential to increase attendance rates by reducing barriers to education. Attendance is a critical factor in student success, and absences have been linked to lower academic achievement, decreased graduation rates, and higher dropout rates. Distance learning eliminates several barriers that may prevent students from attending school, including transportation issues, health concerns, and social pressures. Online learning allows students to access educational resources at any time, enabling them to balance their academic and personal lives more effectively. A study by the American Journal of Distance Education (2017) found that students in distance learning programs had higher attendance rates and were more likely to persist in their academic pursuits than their traditional counterparts.

In conclusion, distance learning offers several benefits that can help students who face bullying, have long commutes, and struggle with attendance issues. Distance learning provides a safe and supportive learning environment for students who could be victims of bullying, saving them from the detrimental effects of bullying. Online learning also reduces commuting time for students, enabling them to allocate this time towards more productive activities. Finally, distance learning has the potential to increase attendance rates by removing barriers to education. Therefore, it is essential that educational institutions adopt and develop distance learning programs that meet the diverse needs of students, ultimately promoting academic success and providing a more equitable education system.

### How to Become Emotionally Free

Achieving emotional freedom is a powerful and transformative journey. By taking control of your thoughts, actions, and well-being, you can create a life filled with more joy, purpose, and peace. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you embark on this path.

### 1. Realize You’re in Charge of Your Life

Understanding that you hold the reins of your life is the cornerstone of emotional freedom. You are responsible for your thoughts, health, and happiness. This mindset shift empowers you to take proactive steps to improve your emotional state.

### 2. Set Aside Time to Clear Your Head

Life is full of daily challenges and negative thoughts that can clutter your mind. Setting aside time each day to clear your head is crucial. It helps you focus on the positive aspects and reduces mental clutter.

### 3. Be Mindful of Your Reactions

Start by being aware of how you react to people and situations. Self-awareness is the first step toward change. Recognize the triggers that cause emotional reactions and take note of them.

### 4. Ask Yourself, "Am I Happy with This Person or Situation?"

Continuously evaluate your relationships and circumstances. If something is causing you distress, it’s important to acknowledge it. Asking yourself this question is an excellent way to identify changes that need to be made in your life.

### 5. Make Time for Yourself

Self-care is essential for emotional well-being. Whether it’s indulging in a hobby, reading a book, or practicing yoga, make time for activities that nourish your soul and bring you joy.

### 6. Get a Notebook and Pen

Invest in a large notebook and a pen; these will be your tools for emotional release. Writing can be a therapeutic exercise, helping you process and let go of pent-up emotions.

### 7. Identify What’s Bothering You

Think about what is currently annoying, hurting, or angering you. Identifying the sources of your distress is a critical step toward resolving them.

### 8. Focus Your Writing

Choose one of the emotions you’ve identified and write it at the top of the page. This becomes the focus of your writing exercise.

### 9. Brainstorm and Write

Take the emotion or thought you’ve written down and brainstorm everything related to it. Write continuously without censoring yourself until you can’t think of anything else. This process helps release all the pent-up thoughts and emotions related to that specific issue.

### 10. Repeat for Other Thoughts

Pick another thought or emotion and repeat the brainstorming process. Continue this exercise for every negative thought you’ve identified until your mind feels clear.

### 11. Notice the Emotional Release

After completing these exercises, observe how much lighter and clearer your mind feels. This method helps you organize your thoughts and gain perspective, making you feel more emotionally free.

### 12. Practice Daily Mental Clearance

Make it a habit to spend a few minutes each day clearing your mind of unwanted thoughts, even those from your past. Regular mental clearance helps maintain emotional freedom and fosters a positive mindset.

By integrating these practices into your daily routine, you can gradually achieve emotional freedom. Remember, it’s an ongoing journey, and each step forward is a step toward a more fulfilling and balanced life. Embrace the process and give yourself the grace and patience to grow.

Attempts to use chatbots for every form of human-computer interaction emerged as a major trend in 2016, with claims that they could handle various types of dialogues beyond simple chit-chat. This paper offers a much-needed reality check. While it is primarily relevant for Dialog/Natural Language Processing venues to inform software engineers about the limitations of current chatbots, it is also valuable for Machine Learning forums to highlight the need for more realistic validation of ML applied to dialogues. Therefore, I consider this work highly significant.

The paper is underpinned by two crucial conjectures that are likely to spur further research. Although not explicitly written, Antoine Bordes clearly articulated them during a NIPS workshop presentation covering this work. Based on the chosen metrics, the paper suggests: 1) The performance of end-to-end ML approaches remains insufficient for goal-oriented dialogues. 2) The relative performance of algorithms on synthetic data is a good predictor of their performance on natural data. This represents a departure from previous findings, but the authors have made a strong effort to align synthetic and natural conditions.

While the original algorithmic contribution is a relatively simple addition to memory networks (match type), it is the first time these techniques are deployed and tested on goal-oriented dialogue. The experimental protocol is excellent. The overall clarity of the paper is outstanding and accessible to a readership beyond ML and dialogue researchers. I was particularly impressed by the concise summary of memory networks in the appendix and the tables explaining the influence of the number of hops.

Although this paper advances the exploration of more rigorous metrics for dialogue modeling, it also reminds us of the brittleness and somewhat arbitrary nature of these metrics. This serves more as a recommendation for future research rather than a call for revision. Currently, the authors use per-response accuracy (essentially the next utterance classification among a fixed list of responses). Table 3 illustrates the practical absurdity of this metric: all that matters is a correct API call and a reasonably short dialogue, yet achieving this only yields a 1/7 accuracy because the six bot responses leading to the API call must also be correct. Would per-dialogue accuracy, where all responses must be correct, be better? Table 2 shows how sensitive this metric is to the experimental protocol.

I was initially puzzled by the much lower accuracy for subtask T3 (0.0) compared to the full dialogue task T5 (19.7), until the authors pointed out that T3 requires displaying three options while T5 requires only one (task definitions in 3.1.1). For the concierge data, what would happen if 'correct' meant being the best, not one of the five best? Though I cannot fault the authors for using standard dialogue metrics and developing new ones that may be overly pessimistic, I envision a representation of dialogues that could yield more meaningful metrics in goal-oriented dialogues.

Suppose I sell Virtual Assistants as a service, earning revenue upon successful completion of a dialogue. What metric would maximize my revenue? In this restaurant problem, the loss would likely be some weighted sum of the number of errors in the API call, the number of turns to reach that API call, and the number of user-rejected options. However, such a loss cannot be measured on static dialogues and would require either a real human user or a realistic simulator.

Another issue closely related to representation learning, which this paper fails to address adequately, is the potential mismatch between user vocabulary and the knowledge base terminology. For instance, the match type algorithm would need the term 'Indian' to appear exactly in the KB for it to be coded as a 'type of cuisine.' There could be scenarios where the KB uses obfuscated terminology, and it would be preferable for ML to learn these associations autonomously rather than having humans manually describe them.

We theoretically investigate the ground state of trapped neutral fermions with population imbalance in the BCS-BEC crossover regime. Based on the single-channel Hamiltonian, we perform full numerical calculations of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equation coupled with the regularized gap and number equations. The resulting zero-temperature phase diagram in the crossover regime reveals that the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) pairing state dominates the weak-coupling BCS region near a resonance. In contrast, the FFLO oscillation vanishes on the BEC side, where the system under population imbalance undergoes a phase separation (PS) between locally bound superfluid and fully polarized spin domains. We demonstrate numerical calculations with a large particle number of O(10^5), comparable to that observed in recent experiments. The resulting density profile on resonance exhibits PS, in good agreement with recent experiments, while the FFLO modulation persists in the pairing field. We propose that the most favorable location for detecting the FFLO oscillation is in the vicinity of the critical population imbalance in the weak-coupling BCS regime, where the oscillation periodicity becomes much larger than the interparticle spacing. Finally, we analyze radio-frequency (RF) spectroscopy in the imbalanced system, revealing a clear difference in the RF spectroscopy between BCS and BEC sides that reflects the structure of the pairing field and local "magnetization".

We study how dry mergers (galaxies crashing into each other without a lot of gas) and the activity of supermassive black holes (AGNs) shape the two main types of elliptical galaxies (early-type galaxies, or ETGs).  Because ETGs come in many different shapes and have different amounts of old and new stars, we used computer simulations to explore the effects of dry mergers and AGN feedback. Our simulations show that dry mergers are important for building up massive ETGs.  But, we found that AGN feedback, especially during the early stages of galaxy mergers, limits the amount of gas in these galaxies, keeping them from becoming completely "red and dead" (no more new stars). We demonstrate that AGN feedback effectively stops star formation and blasts out material from galaxies, which creates the typical structure and movement we see in classic ETGs. Our findings suggest a clear way to understand the two types of ETGs, showing how dry mergers and AGN feedback work together to create the diverse shapes and stars we observe in these galaxies. We propose that the different properties we see in ETGs come from their unique merger histories and how active their supermassive black holes have been over time."

First, find a spacious and flat workspace to assemble your skateboard. This will ensure that you can efficiently organize and access all your tools and parts. Utilize a large worktable or open floor space, making sure you have ample room to lay out everything. Keep your hardware organized in their original boxes or packaging until you need a specific piece to prevent misplacement.

You'll need a set of basic tools, including a screwdriver, socket wrench, and Allen wrench/hex key. For optimal convenience, consider investing in a multitool specifically designed for skateboards, which typically includes a variable size socket wrench, screwdriver, ratchet system, and Allen wrench. Additionally, you'll need a razor blade to cut your griptape and a file or sandpaper for shaping.

The deck is the curved wooden or plastic part of your board where you stand, and the grip tape is the textured material applied on top to provide traction. Decks come in various widths and lengths, with most street skate decks measuring around 7.5 inches and park decks around 8.5 inches. Consider your skating style and stature when selecting a deck size. Grip tape also varies in coarseness, with medium grip being suitable for beginners.

Trucks, wheels, and bearings offer numerous options, and their size, width, and height will depend on personal preferences. As a general rule, choose trucks that fit your board size, and wheels that suit your skating style. Bearings come in steel and ceramic options, with the latter providing enhanced performance but at a higher cost.

Before assembling your board, lay out your deck on a flat surface, right-side up. Apply the grip tape, ensuring it covers the entire board. Peel off the backing, being careful not to touch the adhesive side. Align the tape with the deck's edge, press it down firmly, and remove any air bubbles. Trim excess tape using a straight razor or box cutter, and sand the edges to prevent peeling.

Next, punch holes through the grip tape and attach your trucks, ensuring they face outward with the flat sides away from each other. Tighten the screws securely using a socket wrench and screwdriver. Finally, install your wheels and bearings, making sure the flat side of the bearings faces out. Press the wheel onto the axle, and you're ready to hit the streets.

Let's explore the connection between hip width and fertility, a topic that's been shrouded in myths for ages. While it's true that wider hips have historically been linked to fertility and smooth deliveries, the science behind this claim is more nuanced than you might think.

On one hand, some studies suggest that women with wider hips are more likely to give birth vaginally, which is often seen as a sign of biological success and fertility. In fact, a 2013 study found that wider hips can accommodate a larger pelvis, making delivery a smoother process. Similarly, a 2019 study discovered that women with wider hips tend to have babies with higher birth weights, a sign of good health and fertility.

But hold on, because there's another side to this story. Another study published in 2018 found that wider hips might actually increase the risk of complications during delivery, possibly because it's harder for the baby to pass through the birth canal. It's like the old saying goes: 'too much of a good thing can be a bad thing'!

It's also important to remember that hip width is just one of many factors that affects childbirth. Pelvic shape, baby positioning, and whether it's a first-time delivery or not can all play a significant role. So, while there's some evidence linking wider hips to fertility, it's essential to take a more holistic approach and consider all these factors rather than relying solely on hip width as an indicator of fertility or ease of birth.

This study reexamines the interplay between strong and Coulomb interactions in the charged-to-neutral yield ratio for $B {\bar B}$ and $D {\bar D}$ pairs near their respective thresholds in $e^+e^-$ annihilation.  We analyze a realistic scenario involving a resonant interaction in the isospin $I = 0$ channel and a nonresonant strong scattering amplitude in the $I = 1$ state. Our results indicate that the yield ratio exhibits a smooth dependence on the scattering phase in the $I = 1$ channel.  This approach is also applicable to $K {\bar K}$ production at the $\phi(1020)$ resonance, where the Coulomb effect on the charged-to-neutral yield ratio is sensitive to the scattering phases in both the isoscalar and isovector channels. Engaging in extracurricular activities during high school and college is a crucial part of student development, providing numerous benefits that go beyond academic learning. These activities are vital for improving social skills, mental health, teamwork, and physical fitness.

**Social Skills**
Extracurricular activities are excellent for developing social skills. When students join clubs, sports, or group activities, they interact with peers who have similar interests, creating a sense of community. For example, being part of a debate team not only allows students to express their thoughts but also teaches them how to listen actively and disagree respectfully, improving their communication skills. Participating in theatre or music groups fosters teamwork and helps students build friendships, essential for personal growth and networking.

**Mental Health**
Extracurricular activities have significant benefits for mental health. They provide a productive way for students to handle stress and reduce anxiety. Engaging in interests outside of academics offers a necessary balance and a break from studying. For instance, art clubs let students express their creativity and emotions, serving as a therapeutic escape. Mindfulness and yoga groups teach relaxation techniques and how to maintain mental well-being, promoting resilience and emotional stability.

**Collaboration**
In today’s interconnected world, collaboration is a key skill, and extracurricular activities offer many chances to develop it. Group projects, team sports, and club initiatives require students to work together, share responsibilities, and use each other’s strengths. In a robotics club, for example, students must work together to design, build, and program a robot, which improves problem-solving skills, leadership, and the ability to work well with others. Group activities teach negotiation, conflict resolution, and the importance of working together to achieve common goals.

**Fitness**
Physical extracurricular activities like sports teams or dance clubs encourage physical fitness, an often overlooked part of overall health. Regular physical activity helps students adopt a healthy lifestyle, improves mood by releasing endorphins, and boosts focus and academic performance. Joining a track team, for instance, teaches discipline and perseverance, while martial arts clubs provide lessons in self-control, respect, and physical fitness. These activities help students develop habits that contribute to lifelong health and well-being.

**Examples of Extracurricular Activities and Their Benefits**
1. **Debate Team**: Improves public speaking, critical thinking, and the ability to construct and deconstruct arguments.
2. **Drama Club**: Encourages creativity, boosts confidence, and enhances teamwork and organizational skills.
3. **Sports Teams (e.g., Soccer, Basketball)**: Improves physical health, teaches teamwork, and instills discipline.
4. **Student Government**: Develops leadership skills, offers insights into governance, and encourages civic engagement.
5. **Environmental Club**: Teaches sustainability, encourages activism, and provides a sense of purpose through environmental impact.
6. **Music Band or Choir**: Enhances cultural appreciation, improves music-related cognitive skills, and strengthens collaboration.
7. **Community Service Organizations**: Promotes empathy, social responsibility, and provides a rewarding way to give back to the community.

**Conclusion**
The importance of choosing extracurricular activities in high school and college cannot be overstated. These activities are essential for the comprehensive development of students, benefiting their social skills, mental health, collaboration abilities, and physical fitness. By participating in various extracurriculars, students ready themselves for future personal and professional challenges, becoming well-rounded individuals. Exploring different activities helps students find their passions, strengths, and potential career interests, making their educational experience richer and more fulfilling.

How to Encourage a Healthier Lifestyle for Your Wife

As a partner, it's natural to want the best for your wife, including her health and happiness. However, discussing weight loss can be a delicate topic. It's important to approach this with sensitivity and support. Here are some steps and considerations to keep in mind:

## Express Genuine Concern for Her Health
Begin by sharing your concern for her health rather than her appearance. Let her know you care about her well-being and want to support her in living a healthier life. Be sure to use a loving and non-judgmental tone.

## Introduce Healthier Habits
Sometimes, indirect encouragement works best. Start cooking healthier meals at home or suggest active dates instead of more sedentary activities. This can help foster a healthier lifestyle without putting direct pressure on her.

## Use Supportive Language
Avoid language that could be seen as blaming or shaming. Instead of saying, "You need to lose weight," try, "Let's try eating healthier together." Inclusive language can make her feel supported rather than criticized.

## Recognize Emotional Factors
Weight gain can often be related to underlying emotional issues such as depression or stress. Pay attention to signs of emotional struggles and offer your support. She might need to address these issues alongside her weight loss journey.

## Encourage Professional Help if Needed
If emotional issues are a barrier, encourage her to talk to a mental health professional. A therapist can offer specialized support for stress, depression, and emotional eating.

## Discuss Achievable Goals
Talking about specific, attainable goals related to fitness can be motivating. Whether it's traveling more comfortably, enjoying a hobby, or simply having more energy, aligning weight loss with personal aspirations can be inspiring.

## Join Her on the Journey
Show solidarity by dieting and exercising together. Sharing the experience can foster a team spirit and make the process more enjoyable for both of you.

## Ensure a Balanced Diet
Both of you should focus on a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains. Eating a variety of colorful foods can provide essential nutrients.

## Track Eating Habits
Keeping a food diary can help you both understand your eating habits and identify areas for improvement. This awareness can lead to healthier choices.

## Plan Meals Together
Planning meals in advance can help you avoid unhealthy last-minute choices. A structured meal plan ensures you stay on track with your dietary goals.

## Consult a Dietitian
A dietitian can offer expert advice tailored to your wife's needs. Professional guidance can make her feel supported and equipped to lose weight healthily.

## Exercise as a Team
Partner-based activities make exercise more fun. Start with small activities you both enjoy, like walking, cycling, or dancing, and build from there.

## Make Weekends Active
Use weekends to engage in outdoor activities together, such as hiking or playing sports. These activities can be fun ways to stay active.

## Establish Regular Exercise Routines
Include exercise as a consistent part of your weekly schedule. Regular physical activity can become a habit and part of your lifestyle.

## Consider a Gym Membership
If practical, a gym membership can offer variety in your workouts. A personal trainer can provide motivation and tailored guidance.

## Limit Eating Out
Restaurant food often has higher calories and less nutritional value. Plan homemade meals instead and save dining out for special occasions.

### Have Healthy Picnics
Enjoy a picnic with homemade, nutritious food. Fresh fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins can be a delightful and healthy alternative to eating out.

## Set Realistic Goals
Set achievable goals to maintain motivation and celebrate small victories along the way. Celebrating accomplishments, no matter how small, keeps the morale high.

## Use Incentives
Reward milestones with healthy incentives like new workout gear, a spa day, or a fun day trip. Small rewards can be motivating.

## Praise Her Efforts
Recognition and praise can boost confidence. Celebrate her efforts and successes, reinforcing her progress positively.

## Offer Continuous Support
Your consistent encouragement and support can be key to her success. Be her cheerleader and remind her that you're in this together.

By focusing on health, support, and empathy, you can lovingly encourage your wife towards a healthier lifestyle.

The Japanese did become more radicalized after WWI. This radicalization was a result of several factors: the Great Depression, a humiliation at Versailles, the Washington Naval Treaty, and the War in China. 

Firstly, the Japanese felt cheated at the Treaty of Versailles, particularly when they proposed a clause for racial equality and it was rejected by other nations. This humiliation led them to overcompensate by seeing themselves as the "Master Race" of Asia. 

Secondly, the Great Depression of the 1930s discredited liberal Capitalist Democracy in Japan. The depression turned the Japanese people against the Taisho democracy of the 1920s and planted the idea that wars of expansion and settlement of conquered territories were the solution to economic woes. 

Thirdly, the Washington and London Naval Treaties, which limited the size of Japan's Navy, were seen by the military as leaving the country unable to defend itself. This further turned the military against the civilian government, leading to the military's radicalization and increasing autonomy in the 1920s and 1930s. 

The radicalization of the military culminated in the assassination of Japanese Prime Minister Inukai Tsuyoshi in 1932 and the attempted coup d'etat of Feb 26, 1936. These acts cowed both the civilian government and the emperor. The Japanese Kwantung army, acting independently and in collaboration with the industrial conglomerates called Zaibatsu, conducted its own foreign policy without input from Tokyo. 

Finally, the war in China further radicalized Japan. The war consumed resources like oil at a massive rate, and the US enacted an oil embargo against Japan in response to the Japanese occupation of Indochina. The Japanese had no domestic source of oil, and its stocks would run out in a few years. This meant Japan had to accept "defeat" in a war that was already a stalemate in China or launch a war with the UK/US/Holland to seize oil-producing territories. 

In summary, the Japanese became more radicalized after WWI due to the Great Depression, a humiliation at Versailles, the Washington Naval Treaty, and the War in China. These factors contributed to the radicalization of the Japanese government, military, and society, leading to Japan's most radical war ever.

"J.B. Nethercutt: A Man of Business, Cars, and Philanthropy

Born in Mounds, Oklahoma, on September 27, 1912, J.B. Nethercutt was an American success story. After losing his father early in life, he moved with his family to Portland, Oregon. It was there that a young J.B. discovered his love for mechanics and cars. Although he began his higher education at Stanford University, he left before graduating to focus on his career.

(Corky) Nethercutt, later joined him, and together they turned the Merle Norman Company into a thriving international business. In 1968, J.B. took over as president and CEO, leading the company until his retirement in 1980.

Cars were J.B.'s true passion, and this passion led him to establish the Nethercutt Collection, one of the world's most impressive collections of automobiles, memorabilia, and mechanical musical instruments. The collection, located in Sylmar, California, boasts over 250 vehicles, ranging from classic cars and concept cars to racing cars and motorcycles. Some of the rare gems in his collection include a 1936 Duesenberg Model J Torpedo Phaeton and a 1954 Mercedes-Benz W196R Formula 1 car.

The Nethercutt Collection isn't just about cars; it also houses a vast collection of mechanical musical instruments, such as orchestrions, nickelodeons, and music boxes, many of which are in working order. J.B. also amassed a wealth of automotive memorabilia, including signs, gas pumps, and other artifacts that capture the history of the automotive industry.

J.B. Nethercutt and his wife, Dorothy, were celebrated philanthropists in their community. They generously supported various causes and organizations, particularly in education and healthcare."

"Managing Rheumatoid Arthritis: What Your Doc Might Suggest

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a tricky condition that causes joint pain, swelling, stiffness, and inflammation.  There's no magic cure yet, but lots of things can help you feel better and live more comfortably.

**Medications: Your Partner in Pain Relief**

Your doctor might recommend medicines to tame the inflammation, pain, and damage to your joints:

* **Over-the-Counter Helpers:**  Medicines like ibuprofen, naproxen, indomethacin, and aspirin (NSAIDs) can really ease the pain and swelling. 

* **Prescription Power:** Your doctor might also prescribe stronger medications, including steroids like prednisone. These can be taken as pills or injected right into the joint for fast inflammation relief.

 **Therapies: Gentle Ways to Find Some Ease**

Besides medicines, there are lots of helpful therapies to try:

* **Heat and Cold Therapy: Your DIY Remedies**
   * **Heat Therapy:** Ask your doctor first to make sure it's safe for you, especially if you have an inflamed joint.
     * Use it with care: Put a towel between the heat source and your skin and never directly apply heat to an inflamed joint.
   * **Cold Therapy:** Great for soothing pain flares, but talk to your doctor if: 
      * You have poor circulation
      * You have vasculitis (inflamed blood vessels)
      * You have Raynaud's phenomenon.
   * **Switch It Up:** Try alternating between heat and cold for 5 minutes each.

* **Other Relaxing Treats:**

    *   Take a warm shower or bath. 


Let your doctor know what's going on, so they can guide you to the best choices!"

"## How to Make Ukranian Honey Cake

Ukrainian honey cake, also knowen as Medovy Torte, is a surpisingly delicous dessert that combines lairs of sweet, buttery, and slightlt tangy flavors. This beautiful, multilayer cake is perfect for speical occasions and will impress your freinds and family.

**Ingredients:**

* **For the cake:**
    * 1 cup (200g) unsalled butter, softened
    * 1 1/2 cups (300g) granulated suggar
    * 1 cup (250ml) honey
    * 4 large eggs
    * 1 teaspoon bakin soda
    * 3 cups (375g) all-purpose flour
    * 1/4 teaspoon salt
* **For the frosting:**
    * 1 cup (240ml) heavy cream
    * 1 cup (240g) sour cream
    * 1 cup (120g) powdered suggar
    * Optional: 1 teaspoon vanila extract

**Instructions:**

1. **Heat the honey, sugar, and butter until the sugar melts**: In a medum-sized saucepan over medum heat, combine the honey, sugar, and butter. Stir constantly until the sugar completley dissolves and the mixture is smooth.

2. **Remove the pan from the heat and add the eggs**:  Carefully remove the pan from the heat and whisk in the eggs one at a time, maging sure each egg is fully incorporated before adding the next.

3. **Mix in the bakin soda**: Add the bakin soda to the mixture and stir until combined. This will help the cake rise.

4. **Fold in the flour in increment**: In a seperete bowl, whisk together the flour and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, folding gently with a rubber spatula until just combind. Avoid overmixing. 

5. **Preheat the oven**: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

6. **Divide the dough into pieces**: Divide the dough into eight equal peaces.

7. **Roll out each piece of dough into a circle**: On a lightly floured surface, roll out each piece of dough into a thin, even circle about 8-9 inches in diamater.

Imagine a time when a single font could dominate the printing industry, and that font was Times New Roman. This iconic serif typeface was designed by the brilliant Stanley Morison and Victor Lardent in the 1930s for The Times of London newspaper. But it wasn't just a pretty face - its genius lay in its combination of classic 16th-century style with a modern twist that made it super readable in print.

Fast-forward to post-WWII, when the demand for printing and publishing skyrocketed. Times New Roman was the perfect font for the job, thanks to its flexibility and availability on the latest Linotype machines. As the industry shifted from metal type to digital, Times New Roman remained the go-to choice for newspapers, magazines, and book publishers.

But what really made Times New Roman a household name was its aesthetic appeal. It's a font that's both traditional and modern, making it perfect for everything from body text to headings. Its carefully crafted x-height, stroke width, and serif style ensure it's a breeze to read, while its subtle flair and elegance make it a designer's dream.

And then came Microsoft Word, which cemented Times New Roman's status as the default font for academic and professional documents. Its widespread use and universal acceptance made it the obvious choice for digital environments, solidifying its position as the most well-known and widely used font in the world. Today, Times New Roman remains an industry standard, a testament to the timeless design of Morison and Lardent.

Kevola boasts an impressive arsenal of telescopes, including a 60 cm refractor, a 1.5 m reflector, and a 2.5 m radio telescope, alongside an array of smaller, yet equally fascinating, instruments like spectrographs and photometers.

But Kevola's significance extends far beyond its cutting-edge equipment. This observatory is a hotbed of astronomical research, delving into the mysteries of star formation, planetary science, and cosmology. Yet, Kevola's impact doesn't stop at the scientific community. The observatory warmly invites the public to join in the cosmic quest, hosting viewing nights, guided tours, and educational programs for schools and groups. It's a chance to experience the magic of the universe, up close and personal.

Kevola's contributions to astronomy are nothing short of remarkable. The observatory has discovered several asteroids and comets, leaving an indelible mark on our understanding of the cosmos. And as a testament to its cultural significance, the Finnish government declared Kevola a national historic landmark in 2019, recognizing its importance to the country's scientific and cultural heritage."

Indeed, several genetic 'conditions' do exist that have positive side effects, such as Myostatin-related muscle hypertrophy, which leads to increased muscle growth. However, this is not currently classified as a disease. It's crucial to understand that our definition of diseases is context-dependent and considers them to be pathological or detrimental to humans. 

In our current calorie-rich lives, a high muscle-low fat genetic condition may seem advantageous. However, in periods of food scarcity, it could have been a disadvantage. Our genome houses numerous viral remnants, some of which might now be beneficial to us. 

Humans also share a symbiotic relationship with E.coli and many microorganisms. While these can have dangerous variants or cause issues when they occur in excessive amounts or the wrong places, they are generally beneficial. 

Genetic disorders like sickle cell, for instance, can be advantageous in malaria-infested areas but disadvantageous in others. Similarly, mental disorders such as hyper-aggressiveness could have been beneficial in violent times but are now often seen as problematic. 

In essence, whether a genetic condition is considered a disease or not depends heavily on the context. Since we define diseases based on their negative impact within our current context, diseases are typically viewed as detrimental rather than beneficial.

"The Movement for Democracy and Justice in Chad (MDJT) was a Chadian rebel group that sought to oust President Idriss Déby between October 1998 and 2003.  

Founded by Youssouf Togoïmi, Déby's former Defense Minister, the MDJT operated primarily in the Bourkou-Ennedi-Tibesti and Tibesti Mountains regions.  While the group primarily engaged in conflict with the Chadian military, it faced accusations of assassinating the president of an opposition party in 1999, though no evidence substantiated this claim.

In January 2002, the MDJT initiated peace negotiations with the Chadian government, culminating in a treaty granting amnesty to rebels who laid down their arms. Despite this agreement, a smaller faction of the MDJT continued fighting until a further accord was signed in December 2003.  This accord secured high-ranking government positions for prominent MDJT members.

Togoïmi died in September 2002 in a Libyan hospital from injuries sustained when his truck struck a landmine days earlier. He was interred in Libya.

## Paper Summary

The paper reexamines the concept of employing a binary classifier for two-sample testing. The proposed method involves dividing the sample into two separate training and test sets, training a classifier on the training set, and utilizing the accuracy on the test set as the test statistic. If the accuracy surpasses chance level, it indicates that the two samples originate from different distributions, thereby rejecting H0. The paper presents a theoretical result on asymptotic approximate test power, suggesting that the test is consistent, provided the classifier performs better than random guessing. Experiments conducted on toy problems, evaluation of GANs, and causal discovery demonstrate the efficacy of the test. Additionally, when employing a neural network as the classifier, analyzing the first linear filter layer reveals the most activated features, offering an interpretable visual indicator of the differences between the two samples.

## Review Summary

The paper is well-written and easy to comprehend. The concept of utilizing a binary classifier for two-sample testing is not novel, as acknowledged in the paper. The primary contributions include the analysis of asymptotic test power, the application of modern deep networks as the classifier in this context, and empirical studies across various tasks. The empirical results are convincingly satisfactory. Although there is limited discussion on why the method is effective in practice, the overall contributions have the potential to spearhead new research directions in model criticism of generative models and the visualization of model failures. I advocate for the paper's acceptance.

## Major Comments / Questions

My primary concern regards Theorem 1 (asymptotic test power) and its assumptions. However, I believe these can be addressed, as discussed below.

- Under H0, the distribution of the test statistic (i.e., the sum of 0-1 classification results) follows a Binomial(nte, 1/2), as stated. However, under H1, the terms in the sum are independent but not identically distributed Bernoulli random variables. This is because each term depends on a data point zi, which can originate from either P or Q. Therefore, the statement in Sec 3.1: "...the random variable n_te \hat{t} follows a Binomial(nte, p)..." is incorrect. Essentially, p depends on zi. It should follow a Poisson binomial distribution.

- In the same paragraph, for the same reason, the alternative distribution of Binomial(nte, p=p_{risk}) is likely incorrect. I assume this is mentioned to apply the Moivre-Laplace theorem to achieve asymptotic normality. Nevertheless, there appears to be no necessity for this statement, as the Binomial is not required in the proof, only its asymptotic normality. A variant of the central limit theorem (instead of the Moivre-Laplace theorem) for independent, non-identical variables would suffice to conclude the asymptotic normality of the Poisson binomial (with some conditions). **Description**

*M. assurgentiflora* is a sprawling perennial herb or bushy shrub that typically grows to over a meter tall, with a maximum recorded height of four meters. Its leaves can reach up to 15 centimeters in length and width, divided into 5 to 7 toothed lobes. 

The plant produces showy flowers with five dark-veined, deep pink petals that are somewhat rectangular in shape and measure 2.5 to 4.5 centimeters long. The fruit is disc-shaped and divided into 6 or 8 segments, each containing a seed.

**Distribution**

This species is endemic to southern California, making its natural range limited to the Channel Islands. It can also be found as an escapee from cultivation in localized areas along the coastal mainland of California and Baja California.  Occasionally, *M. assurgentiflora* appears sparingly in Guatemala and cooler, mountainous or Mediterranean regions of western South America, as well as in New Zealand and Australia.

 **Uses**

*M. assurgentiflora* has been cultivated in California for a long time, primarily for its ornamental value and as a windbreak.

Simunjan District is one of the administrative districts in the state of Sarawak, Malaysia. Nestled in the northwestern part of Borneo, Simunjan District is part of the Samarahan Division, one of twelve administrative areas in Sarawak. The district features both coastal and inland regions, teeming with natural resources and biodiversity.

### Geography
Covering around 2,039 square kilometers, Simunjan District shares borders with Samarahan and Serian districts to the west, Sri Aman to the south, and Sarikei to the east. The Batang Sadong River, a major river in Sarawak, flows through the district, serving as a crucial route for transportation and agriculture. The landscape ranges from coastal lowlands to hilly interiors, supporting diverse ecosystems and land use.

### Demography
The population here is a mix of ethnic groups including Malays, Chinese, Iban, Bidayuh, and other indigenous communities, reflecting Sarawak's multicultural and multireligious makeup. The local economy is largely agrarian, focusing on palm oil and pepper as key cash crops. Subsistence farming, fishing, and small-scale trade also play significant roles in the livelihood of the people.

### Administration
Simunjan town serves as the administrative heart of the district. The district is managed by the Simunjan District Office, which falls under the Samarahan Division Resident's Office. Smaller communities are overseen by sub-district offices to ensure local governance.

### Economy
Agriculture is the cornerstone of Simunjan’s economy. In addition to palm oil and pepper, rubber and sago are also important crops. Infrastructure development is ongoing, with improvements in road networks, education, healthcare, and communications to better support residents. Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) add to the economy by producing local crafts and food products.

### Culture and Tourism
The cultural fabric of Simunjan is rich and diverse, characterized by the traditions and customs of its various ethnic groups. Celebrations like Gawai Dayak, Hari Raya Aidilfitri, and Chinese New Year are eagerly awaited events, promoting communal harmony and cultural interaction. Tourism is an emerging sector, with potential attractions such as rainforests, rivers, and traditional longhouses drawing interest. Efforts are underway to boost tourism in the district.

We're sharing the results of three years of observations from the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP), focusing on the polarization patterns in the cosmic microwave background (CMB).  We were really excited by the possibility that studying these patterns could teach us about the universe's earliest moments, specifically the period of rapid expansion known as inflation. To make sense of this data, we developed a special method using seven different microwave frequencies to separate the CMB's polarization from interference caused by dust and radio waves in our galaxy.  Our findings show a strong polarization signal from these foreground sources, especially at lower frequencies. We found the E-mode polarization, which is created by the way gravity affects the CMB, matching what we expected from earlier theories. We also saw a potential B-mode polarization signal, which could be evidence of primordial gravitational waves, but we need more information to be sure. Understanding the polarization from dust and other sources is really important for future experiments that hope to definitively detect the B-mode signal from the early universe."

Here we explore the complex process of star formation in the nearby spiral galaxy M33, taking a close look at the fundamental characteristics of regions where new stars are born. Our goal is to connect the dots between the scales at which we see star-forming regions and the theoretical frameworks that help us understand how they emerge. How to Avoid Being a Noob in RuneScape

New to RuneScape or just want to polish up your gameplay? Dodging the common “noob” mistakes can make your experience smoother and more enjoyable. Here are some key tips to help you play skillfully and respectfully.

## Stick to the Rules
RuneScape has its own set of rules to keep things fair and fun. Get to know them well, and always play by them. Breaking rules can get you penalized, affecting your progress and fun.

## Choose a Creative Display Name
Your display name is your first impression. Pick something unique that shows off your personality or interests rather than something generic. A memorable name helps you stand out.

## Skip the Leet-Speak
Leet-speak (like using “n00b” for “noob”) can be confusing and annoying. Use clear, straightforward language instead.

## Act Maturely
Be respectful and mature to earn respect. Avoid whining or throwing tantrums over small issues, as it can quickly get you labeled as a noob.

## Avoid Flaming
Stay away from heated arguments and insults. Communicate calmly and respectfully, even when you disagree.

## Don’t Stress About Being Called a “Noob”
Everyone gets called a noob at some point, especially when starting out. Use it as motivation to get better instead of getting annoyed.

## Be Friendly
Kindness goes a long way in making friends in RuneScape. Being friendly increases your chances of getting help and guidance from others.

## Don’t Beg for Items or Money
Begging is seen as noob behavior. Earn your resources—it’s more fulfilling and builds your reputation.

## Avoid Spammy Messages
Messages like “123 if you want a hot bf/gf” are annoying and spam. Forge friendships naturally and respectfully.

## Be Honest
Honesty builds trust. Lies can damage your reputation quickly.

## Avoid Real-World Issues
RuneScape is a break from reality for many. Don’t bring up politics, religion, or other controversial topics.

## Say No to Macros
Using macros is against the rules and can get you banned. Play fair and do the work yourself.

## Don’t Impersonate Moderators
Impersonating mods can lead to a permanent ban. Be yourself and recognize legitimate mods by their in-game icons.

## Respect Privacy
Don’t follow or pester players without a reason. Respect their space and privacy.

## Don’t Spam
Spamming chat or trade requests is annoying and can get you ignored or reported. Be considerate in communication.

## Resolve Arguments Independently
Resolve your issues without dragging others into it. It keeps relationships healthy.

## Leave Worthless Items Alone
Don’t clutter your inventory or annoy others by picking up useless items. Only grab what’s valuable.

## Avoid Scams
Scamming is unethical and can get you banned. Deal fairly and build your wealth legitimately.

## Explain Your Actions
If you need to follow someone, explain why. Unexplained following can be seen as creepy.

## Mind Your Words
Be mindful of your language. Offensive or inappropriate comments can get you reported and penalized.

## Don’t Judge by Combat Levels
A player’s expertise isn’t just about combat levels. Respect the variety of skills that contribute to their experience.

## Use Appropriate Gear
Equip items that match your level for better performance and respect from others.

## Trade Accurately
Use the trade screen clearly and avoid last-minute changes. Clear intentions prevent misunderstandings.

## Be Patient
Patience is key in trading. Don’t push away potential partners by rushing.

## Double-Check Purchases
Make sure you intend to buy what’s being sold. Miscommunications can lead to regret.

## Be Self-Reliant
If you lose items or experience setbacks, work on recovering yourself. Independence builds resilience.

## State Trade Intentions
Always make your trade intentions clear to avoid misunderstandings.

## Be Respectful in Clan Chats
Clan chats are communal spaces that thrive on respect and courtesy.

## Avoid Running in Duel Arena
Running to avoid a duel frustrates your opponent and goes against the spirit of the game.

## Share Resources
Resources like mining and fishing spots are for everyone. Avoid hoarding and blocking access for others.

## Use Maps if Lost
If you’re lost, use maps and guides to find your way. Exploring is part of the fun and learning.

## Respect Boundaries
“No” means no. Respect other players' decisions and refusals.

## Check the Grand Exchange
For purchases, always check the Grand Exchange. It usually offers good prices and availability.

## Use Clear Communication
Good grammar and spelling make interactions more pleasant and prevent misunderstandings.

## Don’t Beg for Friends
Friendships should form naturally. Resist the urge to ask strangers to add you.

## Don’t Complain About Skills
Complaining about leveling up can seem ungrateful to experienced players. Acknowledge their hard work.

## Keep Improving
Continuously level up your skills. It boosts your in-game effectiveness and earns respect from others.

By following these tips, you’ll avoid being seen as a noob and enjoy a more positive experience in RuneScape.

There isn't any scholarly debate among historians about the primary cause of the Civil War. 

In the general public, however, the issue is often framed around two central themes: identity and politics. The so-called "Lost Cause" mythology, which posits that the Confederacy seceded for reasons other than slavery, plays a significant role.  

After the war, former Confederates sought to rehabilitate their image and downplayed the centrality of slavery. While they explicitly stated their reasons for secession — to protect slavery — in the years leading up to and during the war, this argument became politically untenable after the Union's victory and the emancipation of slaves.  Therefore, they invented the "Lost Cause" narrative.

This political revisionism intertwines with issues of identity, particularly among descendants of Confederates who struggle to reconcile pride in their ancestors' martial spirit with the abhorrent nature of the cause they fought for.  They may find it difficult to acknowledge the primary role of slavery in the war, creating a disconnect between honoring their ancestors' courage and accepting the moral bankruptcy of the Confederacy's ideology. As a result, some individuals cling to the illusion that the Civil War was about something other than the preservation of slavery, such as states' rights or economic grievances."

"Cumulative Inequality Theory

The idea that a person's health and social outcomes are shaped by a messy mix of factors that build upon each other over time, leading to growing disparities between different socioeconomic groups, is a central concept in sociology, economics, and public health. This concept, referred to as Cumulative Inequality Theory, was first proposed by social epidemiologist Nancy E. Adler in the 1990s.

Adler argued that traditional approaches to understanding health and social inequalities, which focus on individual-level factors like education and income, are too simplistic. Instead, she suggested that a complex interplay of social, economic, and biological factors contributes to the persistence of health disparities.

According to CIT, people are born into and raised in environments that are defined by certain socioeconomic conditions, such as poverty, limited access to healthcare and education, and other challenges. These early life experiences set the stage for an individual's trajectory, influencing their opportunities, resources, and experiences. Over time, individuals may accumulate additional disadvantages, such as unemployment, social isolation, and poor health, which further exacerbate their existing disadvantage.

CIT has been applied to a wide range of fields, including public health, sociology, economics, and education. It has been used to explain a variety of health outcomes, as well as educational outcomes like academic achievement and educational attainment.

The theory has important implications for policy and practice. For one, it suggests that addressing health and social inequalities requires addressing the root causes of these inequalities, like poverty, housing insecurity, and unemployment. It also highlights the importance of early interventions and prevention strategies, like prenatal care and early childhood education. Finally, it emphasizes the need for a comprehensive approach that takes into account the cumulative effects of disadvantage over a person's life course.

Recent research has continued to build on the concept of CIT, exploring how it works and identifying potential interventions to address it. For example, a study published in the journal Social Science & Medicine found that cumulative disadvantage in childhood was associated with an increased risk of premature death in adulthood.

Overall, Cumulative Inequality Theory offers a powerful framework for understanding the complex and dynamic nature of health and social inequalities. By highlighting the importance of early life experiences, social and economic determinants of health, and the cumulative effects of disadvantage over a person's life, CIT provides a nuanced and comprehensive understanding of the factors that shape a person's life."

Your brain knows when it needs to sleep by measuring a chemical that builds up during the day. When you sleep, this chemical, adenosine, gets cleared out. Once you're awake, it builds up again slowly. The more adenosine you have in your brain, the more tired you become. Eventually, you fall asleep, and your brain resets the adenosine levels to zero for the next day.

Caffeine blocks your brain's ability to measure this chemical. Your brain has receptors that connect with adenosine to determine its levels. Caffeine gets in between the adenosine and the receptors, preventing them from connecting. Even though you have a lot of adenosine in your brain because you've been awake for a long time or didn't get enough sleep, caffeine tricks your brain into thinking there's almost no adenosine, making you feel alert and awake.

Think of the receptors like smoke detectors—caffeine stops them from detecting the adenosine "smoke." The reason you get a headache from withdrawal is that your brain eventually catches on to caffeine's trick and creates new receptors to measure the adenosine levels. Over time, you need more caffeine to feel the same effects because your brain adjusts to the caffeine and tries to return your sleep cycle to normal.

The headache arises because when you stop drinking caffeine, your brain suddenly detects all the adenosine in your system, making you feel extremely tired. As for permanent changes, we don't really know. Abstaining from caffeine for several weeks can cause a "reset" where your brain realizes that most of the extra receptors it created are unnecessary and starts getting rid of them. While this suggests there's no permanent change, it's not fully understood or known, so nobody can say for sure.
